minutes.headline: DPU heard public comment on Unitil's electric and gas rate requests in Fitchburg; no ruling, speakers overwhelmingly opposed.
minutes.summary: The Department of Public Utilities held a public hearing on Fitchburg Gas and Electric (Unitil) petitions for electric and gas base distribution rate increases, including a five-year performance-based ratemaking plan. After DPU and company statements, the Attorney General's office, legislators, city officials and many residents spoke against the increases. The commission made no decisions and said it would rule in writing later.

decisions.decision: The DPU has suspended the effective date of any new rates to July 1, 2024 while it investigates.
Two additional public hearings are scheduled over Zoom for November 29th, at 2 p.m. and 7 p.m.; evidentiary hearings are set for February 2024.
The chair said the DPU will open a new proceeding in the coming weeks on affordability, including income-based discounts.

what_happened.line: The Department of Public Utilities held a public hearing in Fitchburg on Unitil's electric and gas base rate increase petitions and made no ruling.
The DPU has suspended the effective date of any new rates to July 1, 2024 while it investigates.
Two more public hearings are set over Zoom for November 29 at 2 p.m. and 7 p.m.; evidentiary hearings are set for February 2024.
The Attorney General's office, legislators, city officials and many residents spoke against the increases, citing bill burden and hardship.
The chair said the DPU will open a new proceeding in the coming weeks on affordability, including income-based discounts.

why_it_matters: Unitil's petitions would raise base distribution charges on electric and gas bills, and the decision is made by the state commission, not by a local vote.
Municipal buildings such as libraries are billed in commercial classes with demand charges, so a rate change reaches town and library budgets as well as household bills.
watch_next: Zoom public hearings on November 29 at 2 p.m. and 7 p.m.
Evidentiary hearings in February 2024; new rates cannot take effect before July 1, 2024.
